text: Seminar S1. Round 2 showed that idea 10's certificates are vacuous and idea 11's curvature loses a factor 2; idea 21 claims the kernel has a second, mirror positivity whose spectrum is the primes. QUESTION FOR THE SEMINAR: what exactly would a bridge from mirror positivity on the integers to the shift inequality (Weil positivity) have to say, where must it use that the lattice is the integers and not a Beurling system, and is it true in the two-prime model?

COMPUTED (rh/experiments/e21_reflection/mirror.log, double precision, one implementation): the mirror matrix [c(ab)], a,b = 2..12, of the log-derivative coefficients is non-negative for zeta (rank 5), zeta*L(chi_4), zeta(2s) and L(chi_4) alone, and has negative eigenvalues for the Davenport-Heilbronn impostor (-12.8) and the theta dial at n = 1.2, 1.4, 1.8 (-7.4, -14.2, -8.4), n = 3 (-608) and n = 4 (-58, exactly one negative eigenvalue). Full statement and what is not known: docs/IDEAS.md idea 21.

What is the weakest precise statement of the form 'mirror positivity + something about the Gamma kernel + something about the integers implies the even and odd block inequalities on a window' that is NOT already false for a Beurling system? If you think no such statement can exist, what is the obstruction, stated as mathematics?

DIRECTION OF THE BRIDGE. PROOF_parity_index Lemma 2 writes RH as UPPER bounds on the form of the kernel K: even f: N(f) <= 2<f,c>^2; odd f: N(f) <= -2<f,s>^2. In the one-variable theorem idea 21 cites (Kallen-Lehmann), mirror positivity of a kernel k yields that k(x-y) is positive definite, which is a LOWER bound on its shift form. Please write the conclusion of your bridge as ONE displayed inequality between forms built from K, the diagonal constant c_inf and the two pole functionals: which kernel has its shift form taken, and on which side of the inequality does it stand?

SMALLEST CASE, typed into a computer. Before two primes: ONE prime. System = atoms (log 2) 2^(-k/2) at k log 2, the same w(u) = sum_m e^(-(2m+1/2)u), the same pole. Its mirror matrix is (one rank-one square) + (arch), so it passes your test. (a) What exactly is 'the shift inequality on that lattice' (idea 21, field 'smallest'): a matrix indexed by which points, with which entries, and where do the diagonal self-energy and the pole enter? The lead noted in N25 that on atoms the Weil form is 'trivially positive (infinite self-energy)'. (b) With that definition, is the shift inequality true for the one-prime system on every window, or does it fail at some L (N27: with NO atom it fails from L = 0.362)? (c) If it fails, which hypothesis of the bridge does the one-prime system violate?

WHAT WOULD CHANGE YOUR MIND. Idea 21, new input (2): the mirror matrix is non-negative 'for an Euler product, exactly when all local roots are real with positive multiplicity'. Idea 21, claim: mirror positivity 'holds for every member ... whose zeros lie on its centre line and fails for every member whose zeros do not'. These are two different properties. Control that separates them: F = L(s,chi) L(s,chi-bar), chi the character mod 5 with chi(2) = i (real coefficients, functional equation, Euler product, complex local roots at p = 2, 3 mod 5). What is the entry c(4) at a = b = 2 of its mirror matrix, and what is its smallest eigenvalue on a, b = 2..12? If it comes out negative, which of the two quoted sentences do you keep, and is the mirror test then a test about zeros or a test about local roots?

TWO RESULTS THAT DISAGREE IN WORDS. Your D4: the prime atoms are NOT reflection positive for x -> -x (witness with generic x0, value -(log p)/sqrt p; boxes at L = 1: 9 of 20 eigenvalues negative, smallest -1.12). Your wall W-curv-3: 'primes reflect coordinatewise, Gamma reflects totally'. Your refuter (R9): the matrix [w(log ab) + Lambda(ab)/sqrt(ab)], 2 <= a, b <= 60, has smallest eigenvalue -2.1e-16, and -0.475 at the rationals 3/2, 4/3; he reads D1 as positivity for the TOTAL inversion on log-integer points. Please restate W-curv-3 in the form you would defend now, as a statement a program can check: positive on which set of points or test functions, negative on which, and for the window L = 1 (folded variable x in (0, 1]) how many of the positive points lie inside it?

ARE THESE THE SAME QUANTITY? Theorem B3, third sum (the 'open paths: window edge' term): pairs of jumps a, b with x+a and x+a+b inside the window and x+b outside. Theorem D5: N_even(f) - N_odd(f) = 4 x (Hankel form of K at phi), pairing phi(x) phi(y) through K(x+y), x, y in (0, L]. Both are what is left when a translation-invariant kernel meets a boundary. Is there an identity that writes the open-path term as a Hankel-type (mirror) form, for example after reflecting at the window edge x = L instead of at 0? If you do not know: which single computation on your L = 1, M = 40 matrices would decide it, and what number would mean 'unrelated'?

WHERE IS THE OBSTRUCTION, AND DOES IT USE THE INTEGERS? Your P5 result: locality radius R* = n - 1 in every case, 'forbidding only the most spread-out triples (0, j, n-1) already kills every certificate' (slack -5.8, -3.2, -2.3, -1.4, -0.82 for n = 2, 3, 4, 6, 8), and the same for the Beurling control at L = 0.5. The triple (0, j, n-1) has its two outer boxes at separation 2L, the largest argument at which the kernel K is ever evaluated on the window, and the largest value of x+y in the mirror form. (a) In the infeasible program, is the pair (0, n-1) at the two window ends the only pair that needs a third scale, or do interior pairs fail as well once those triples are removed? (b) Lemma E proves this only 'for R = 0 at a critical window': what is the exact statement you believe for R = n - 2? (c) Since zeta and Beurling give the same R*, does anything in your five lemmas and Theorem F use that the atoms sit at log n, n an integer? Name the line if so.

CONNECTING YOUR BLOCKS TO THE MIRROR FORM. Your Lemma 2: even f: N(f) <= 2<f,c>^2; odd f: N(f) <= -2<f,s>^2. S1-curv's D5: for phi on (0, L] with even and odd extensions f_e, f_o: N(f_e) - N(f_o) = 4 x Hankel_K(phi). By D3 the Hankel form of the Gamma kernel alone is >= 0, so as long as no prime power lies below e^(2L) one has N(f_o) <= N(f_e) for every phi. (a) On such a phi, does either of your two block inequalities follow from the other, and if not, what exactly is the missing term? (b) You found that without primes it is the ODD block that turns negative between L = 0.37 and 0.38 while the even block stays positive (0.00105 at 0.38). Is that asymmetry explained by the sign of the Hankel form, or is it a separate fact? (c) In your three proof files, is there any step that uses that the atoms sit at logs of INTEGERS (Theorem U says 'the positions need not be logarithms of integers')?

THE QUESTION NOBODY WANTS, about B3. The proof of Theorem D1 reads: Lambda(ab) != 0 with a, b >= 2 forces a = p^i, b = p^j, so the matrix is 'a direct sum over p of (log p) v_p v_p^T ... this is the Euler product of -zeta'/zeta'. So in your template 'mirror positivity + something about the Gamma kernel + something about the integers => block inequalities' the three hypotheses read: has an Euler product with real local roots; has this Gamma factor; its atoms sit at integers. Is that list different from the sentence 'F is zeta'? If it is not different, what do you expect a proof to USE from the mirror FORM that it could not use from the bare fact of an Euler product, i.e. which operation on the kernel becomes available that was not available before (owner rule 2: name the new input)? And which number, if it came out differently in the two-prime model, would make you drop the bridge?

Three honest answers. (1) For zeta's own Gamma factor and conductor 1 it is NOT different: degree 1, Euler product and that functional equation already force F = zeta (Hamburger; Conrey-Ghosh for the Selberg class, from memory). So at zeta the criterion classifies nothing; its content is only across families (the dial, other Gamma factors). And there it is the wrong invariant in general: I expect your control B6 to FAIL the mirror test, because L(chi)L(chi-bar) mod 5 has local roots i and -i at p = 2, so c_4 = 2 log 2 cos(pi) = -2 log 2 sits on the diagonal of the mirror matrix, although GRH is expected for it. So the mirror test detects real local roots, not zeros on the line; idea 21's claim that it tracks RH along the dial holds there only because the dial's Euler-product members happen to have real roots. I will correct the idea's entry. (2) What it lets a proof use that the bare Euler product did not: so far, nothing proved. The Euler product classically gives a SIGN (Lambda >= 0). The mirror form gives a GRAM representation: a Hilbert space on which multiplication by each integer is a self-adjoint operator, with joint spectrum the primes and the trivial zeros. That is a structure in search of a theorem; by rule 2 it is not yet an idea unless the bridge exists. (3) The number that would make me drop the bridge: in the two-prime model, compute the lowest eigenvalue of each parity block (a) with the true weights, (b) with the weight at 4 flipped to -log 2, which breaks mirror positivity and nothing else, (c) with log 2 replaced by log 2.1. If the sign of the lowest eigenvalue in (a) and (b) is the same on every window up to L = 1, mirror positivity plays no role in the shift inequality and I drop it. If (a) and (c) cannot be separated either, the model cannot see the integers and tests nothing.
